candidate.blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential — preoperative assessment and interpretation of risk-related findings
candidate.blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — ASA physical status
candidate.educational_objective: Interpret ASA Physical Status as a classification of preoperative physical health and systemic disease burden rather than a stand-alone outcome predictor.

options.A: The technical experience of the surgical and anesthesia teams.
options.B: The insurance authorization category for the procedure.
options.C: The client's preoperative physical health status and severity of systemic disease.
options.D: A complete prediction of postoperative outcome based only on procedure type and duration.

candidate.rationale: The ASA Physical Status Classification categorizes a patient's overall preoperative physical health, ranging from a healthy patient to progressively severe systemic disease and moribund status. It is associated with perioperative risk but is not, by itself, a complete outcome-prediction model. C is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: ASA Physical Status classifies the patient's preoperative physical condition/systemic disease severity; it is not a complete stand-alone prediction of operative outcome.
candidate.source_document_title: American Society of Anesthesiologists Physical Status Classification System
candidate.source_locator: ASA Physical Status Classification table and discussion of intended use/limitations
candidate.source_organization: National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI), StatPearls
candidate.stem: Before surgery, the nurse reviews the client's ASA Physical Status classification. What does this classification primarily describe?
